title: Gill says India will play four pacers in Wellington as New Zealand Test series nears
dek: The captain is choosing between debutant Gurnoor Brar and Prasidh Krishna, and says Rishabh Pant plays. India, fourth in the World Test Championship, need to win most of their last seven Tests.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India will go into the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington on Thursday with four fast-bowling options and a single spinner, captain Shubman Gill said on Tuesday, with the uncapped Gurnoor Brar competing with Prasidh Krishna for a place in the attack.

"We definitely want four fast-bowling options, but we are still deciding which are those fast bowlers," Gill told reporters ahead of the match. He said the choice between Brar and Krishna would depend on who "can give us more for the five days", and that India wanted pace, a consistent line and length and one spinner to hold an end. "There is no dilemma on Rishabh Pant," he added, confirming that the wicketkeeper-batter, back from injury, will play without having had a first-class match on the tour.

## The squad

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) added Brar, 26, to the Test squad on Saturday, a maiden call-up; he was the leading wicket-taker in the ODI series at the time, with nine wickets. He has 71 first-class wickets in 22 matches. Kuldeep Yadav was released, the BCCI said, "in order to play the ongoing domestic cricket back in India". Pant was declared fit after rehabilitation at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence.

India's squad: Shubman Gill (captain), KL Rahul (vice-captain), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Sai Sudharsan, Rishabh Pant, Dhruv Jurel, Ravindra Jadeja, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep, Prasidh Krishna, Anshul Kamboj and Gurnoor Brar.

New Zealand, led by Tom Latham, will be without Mitchell Santner, their white-ball captain, who fractured his right hand in the fifth ODI; all-rounder Dean Foxcroft replaces him. India won that match at Mount Maunganui on Sunday by 22 runs, defending 209 two days after being bowled out for 89 in the fourth game, to take the ODI series 3-1. Arshdeep Singh, who took three for 30, was player of the match.

## What is at stake

The two-Test series counts towards the 2025-27 World Test Championship. New Zealand top the table and India are fourth. Gill said India needed to win "five to six" of their remaining seven Tests to reach the final, and that winning both matches in New Zealand would give them a very good chance. The second Test is in Christchurch. After this series, New Zealand travel to Australia for four Tests starting on 9 December in Perth.

## What happens next

The first Test begins on Thursday, 19 November, at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.
